entries.name: CABAL_FLAGS
entries.notes: ingest/build-all.sh does not read it. It only passes its environment to build-model.py. The make variable CABAL_FLAGS in ingest/Makefile is a different thing: line 18 assigns it empty with ':=', so a value from the caller's environment does not reach the 'cabal test' commands at lines 136 and 144. Measured with GNU Make 4.3 and a scratch makefile outside the checkout: when the caller's environment has the name and the makefile assigns it empty, the recipes see an empty value. So only the build-all-coverage recipe gives build-model.py a non-empty CABAL_FLAGS when make starts the script. A direct run of ingest/build-all.sh passes the caller's value to build-model.py unchanged.

entries.default: Unset or empty: the recipe stops with the shell error 'COVERAGE_BASELINE not set'.
entries.effect: It is the lowest accepted Haskell expression coverage of the ingest tests. The recipe rounds the measured percentage to the nearest 5 and fails when the result is below this value.
entries.name: COVERAGE_BASELINE
entries.notes: The recipe compares with '[ "$ROUNDED" -lt "$BASELINE" ]' and does not check that the value is an integer. With a non-integer value that test reports an error, the shell takes the else branch, and the recipe prints PASS. Confirmed again in this verification with dash, which is /bin/sh on the analysis host: it printed 'Illegal number' and then took the else branch. .github/workflows/ingest-coverage.yml:32 sets it to 35 (outside this area).
entries.values: An integer percentage, for example 35.

entries.name: CPUAFFINITY
entries.notes: The name appears only in these two files of the checkout. Not determined from the checkout: what systemd and taskset do when the variable is unset or empty, and how systemd splits the braces form into arguments. systemd and taskset are not in the checkout. The unit sets SyslogIdentifier=rinzler (line 64) so that the journal does not show taskset as the program name (comment at line 63). The unit comment at line 20 says platformd writes the instance environment file. The checkout does not show which names platformd writes there, except RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH (README.stats.md:46). Confidence is medium because the unset behaviour and the writer of the value are outside the checkout.

entries.default: Unset or empty: CMake searches only the listed names: ghc-9.12.2 (outside Nix only), then ghc-9.12, then ghc. It searches the normal program search path and $HOME/.ghcup/bin. ingest/build-model.py:481 uses the text ghc when the variable is unset.
entries.effect: In CMake the value is a last candidate only: a listed name that is found wins. CMake keeps the path that it finds in the cache variable GHC_EXECUTABLE. ingest/build-model.py without --ingest-bin runs 'cabal run ... -w <GHC>' with the value.
entries.name: GHC
entries.notes: Outside Nix the program that is found must report version 9.12.2 with --numeric-version, or configure fails (ingest/CMakeLists.txt:275-293). The read happens only when BUILD_INGEST_MODELS is ON and TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE is empty (ingest/CMakeLists.txt:39 and :204 return earlier). The comment at flake.nix:1876 says the variable points cmake to the Nix GHC and prevents the use of ghcup. With the measured behaviour the listed names win and $HOME/.ghcup/bin stays in the search list. The dev shell value ghc is already a listed name. Reader outside this area: ingest/build-model.py:481.

readers.mechanism: find_program(GHC_EXECUTABLE NAMES ${INGEST_GHC_NAMES} ENV GHC PATHS $ENV{HOME}/.ghcup/bin); 'ENV GHC' stands inside the NAMES list

default, tools and cuda dev shells; the comment says it points cmake to the Nix GHC and prevents use of ghcup

entries.values: Name or full path of the GHC (Haskell compiler) program. In ingest/CMakeLists.txt:253 the words 'ENV GHC' stand inside the NAMES list of find_program. The CMake manual describes 'ENV var' only after HINTS and PATHS. Result measured with CMake 3.22.1 in a scratch test outside the checkout: CMake tries the value as one more program name, after all listed names. A bare name and a full path both work. A directory does not work. ingest/build-model.py:481 passes the value to 'cabal run -w <ghc>'.
